Outcomes of a gate decision
{{o.g}}{{o.name}}

{{o.what}}

Every phase produces or updates a named document. A document is drafted in the chat (the agent proposes, the person inserts), consolidated in a working document on the page, validated by a person, submitted as one pull request per document and per change, and reviewed at the gate. Agents never write a document or merge anything on their own.

States of a document

{{x.t}}

{{x.d}}

Phase × document × role
DocumentPhaseGateSourceDialogues with the agentValidates and submitsReviews at the gate
{{r.title}}
{{r.sections}}
{{r.phase}}{{r.gate}}{{r.src}}{{r.dialog}}{{r.validates}}{{r.reviews}}
Parallel changes and documents

Same document

Two changes hold a working document for the same DD layer or portfolio ASD. Seen when the document opens and at every gate. Answers: Sequence, Merge, Split.

Same element

Two changes touch the same SBB or contract. Seen at Validate, on the preview build of the pull request. The gate does not pass until decided.

Base moved

The other change merged while this one was drafted. Rebase by section: a three-way merge, the person chooses where they diverge; the document goes back to Working.

Knowledge base

Published elements and documents are nodes keyed by their Git reference (repository, path, sha). A working document is its own node, with a supersedes edge to the published one, until its pull request merges. The assistant answers from what is published first and says when a change in progress proposes something else; it never presents a draft as current.

TOGAF Phase H classifies each change request. In the toolbox the owner picks the class in step 1; it decides who approves and how much of the ASD is needed.

ClassExamplesStepsWho approvesASD
{{c.name}}{{c.ex}}{{c.steps}}{{c.who}}{{c.asd}}

Decisions are Checkpoints (INV-12): a person records them, never an agent. Automated writes to Git go through CTX-INT (INV-07). The "view as" chips above the prototype switch between these roles on the review page.

RoleCanCannot
{{r.role}}{{r.can}}{{r.cannot}}

Several changes can be open on the same application at once. They can collide at three levels; each level has its own guard, and most of the work is preventing collisions rather than resolving them.

LevelExampleCaught byWhen
{{p.level}}{{p.ex}}{{p.by}}{{p.when}}
